title.narrative: Life-saving emergency assistance to vulnerable food insecure farming households in conflict and flood-affected areas

description.narrative: The primary objective of FAO’s proposed intervention is to urgently support food production and food security of the most vulnerable households, targeting smallholder farmers, with a priority on women-headed households, households with pregnant and lactating women (PLW) and women of reproductive age (WRA), households with disabled people, and other vulnerable groups affected by the overlapping crises of conflict and recent flooding in Myanmar. FAO aims to provide immediate life-saving assistance through:• Provision of paddy seeds, compound fertilizer, and organic compost fertilizer to 2,100 of the most vulnerable farming households (10,500 people) to support local food production and restore/sustain livelihoods;• Provision of oil seeds (groundnut and sesame), compound fertilizer, and organic compost fertilizer to 1,400 of the most vulnerable farming households (7,000 people) to strengthen food security and improve nutritional intake and livelihoods;• Provision of unconditional cash assistance (Cash+ approach) to 3,500 of the most vulnerable farming households (17,500 people), enabling households to meet their immediate food and livelihood/other farming needs, or address any unavoidable household expenditures.• Provision of effective awareness orientation during the distributions on appropriate cultivation techniques for certified seed / improved varieties, integrated nutrient and pest management, and nutrition along with FAO already designed leaflets. These interventions are expected to result in enabling the targeted vulnerable households to meet their basic food and livelihood needs thus safeguarding their food security and livelihoods and preventing them from slipping further into higher levels of food insecurity and malnutrition. It will also contribute to the chances of assisted households to adopt negative coping actions and accelerate recovery at the community level. Besides transfer of knowledge, FAO Myanmar's localization agenda emphasizes local partners to build their capacity and enhance local ownership that leads to sustainability of intervention. FAO has worked with several Local partners (LPs) operating in the targeted areas and aim to capitalize on these partnerships.
